newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany must hit deficit target for EMU - Kuehbacher. [CORRECTED 12:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Germany must hit deficit target for EMU - Kuehbacher. [CORRECTED 12:15 GMT]

text.p: Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher on Monday said Germany should not take part in the first round of Europe's currency union if its budget deficit is far above three percent (corrects to add word "far").

"If the budget deficit is far above the three percent level (corrects to add word "far"), then Germany should absolutely not take part at the start of the euro," Kuehbacher, also head of the state central bank in Berlin and Brandenburg, told the newspaper Berliner Morgenpost.

He was referring to the requirement that European Union member nations aim for budget deficits of no more than three percent of their gross domestic product in 1997 in order to join the currency union at its scheduled 1999 launch.
He also said Germany currently was not meeting that criterion and was sceptical whether Finance Minister Theo Waigel could succeed in fulfilling this requirement.
"It is questionable whether Waigel will succeed," Kuehbacher told the paper.
At the weekend, Waigel said the Maastricht Treaty's three percent reference limit meant "3.0 percent" and on Monday said Germany would meet its official 2.9 percent budget deficit target this year.

The quibbling over exactly what "three" means has become a central point of political debate on the EMU in Germany as high unemployment and fragile growth place a question mark over Bonn's ability to meet the deficit target this year.
